2. His extreme weight was due to massive fluid retention (edema) and severe, lifelong obesity. 
3. Anorexia nervosa is an eating disorder characterized by an abnormally low body weight, an intense fear of gaining weight, and a distorted perception of weight. 
4. Minnoch's condition was the exact opposite of anorexia nervosa; he suffered from extreme overeating and morbid obesity, not self-starvation or emaciation.
